seed_variation.verdict: Only one seed was run, so there is no seed variation to measure.
seed_variation.why: A hosted LLM cannot be seeded: our seeds only reach local random generators, and the provider's sampling (temperature etc.) is fixed for this model. So every run can give different text, and the spread across seeds measures the model's own run-to-run variation. Each seed repeats every API call. Each seed sets Python random, NumPy and torch. PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed to the FIRST seed for the whole run.

predictions.SY0103a: The team discussed technical constraints, agreeing that speech recognition should be on-device with a limited fixed vocabulary. They debated costs, chose a brand wake word, added a physical stop button, and considered power options. They agreed the device should provide short audio responses and support multiple timers. Finally, the project manager assigned action items to prepare for the functional design meeting.
predictions.SY0103b: The team began their functional design meeting, noting Tomasz's absence due to the flu postponed their cost breakdown. They recapped decisions regarding on-device speech recognition for a small command set, a wake word, a stop button, and spoken confirmations, while deciding the alarm should get progressively louder. Moving to product naming, they discarded Pepper due to cooking conflicts and selected Kiko as the working name, with Priya agreeing to test it against kitchen sentences. Priya also pitched a two-digit display for remaining minutes, but the team parked this idea and the power source question until they review the cost breakdown with Tomasz. Finally, Laura assigned action items and wrapped up the meeting.
predictions.SY0103c: The project manager reviewed basic pricing, component costs, and the decision to use USB-C power with a two-digit LED display. The user interface designer presented the command list and preliminary wake word testing for Kiko, which showed minor false triggers on cocoa that the team agreed to keep and have the chip supplier tune. The marketing expert then reviewed competitors, noting that the device's lack of wifi and apps is a strong selling point for privacy that supports the twenty-five euro price. Finally, the industrial designer proposed a round, palm-sized puck design featuring a smooth plastic shell, a large rubber top button with a central display, and an agreement to explore color options for future meetings.
predictions.SY0103d: The team reviewed the physical model, settling on two colorways and a white LED display while confirming the unit cost. They evaluated the design against core requirements, noting hands-free usability, an eighty-five decibel ramping alarm, and a competitive twenty-five dollar price point driven by offline functionality. Finally, they assigned action items for testing, documentation, and launch preparations before concluding the meeting.
predictions.SY0110a: Priya, Tom, and Jonas finalized the initial design requirements for the reusable coffee cup, confirming dishwasher safety and standard lid sizes. Tom took on researching durable materials under three euros, while Jonas agreed to investigate return processes and existing deposit systems. Priya will brief Marta on speaking with cafe owners at the upcoming fair. The team briefly touched upon the issue of lost cups and scheduled the next functional design meeting for shortly after.
predictions.SY0110b: The team reviewed material options, selecting polypropylene with a ninety millimeter rim and dropping silicone, while arranging to test samples in a commercial dishwasher at Café Lindner. They also discussed cup return processes, agreeing on a counter return method without dedicated machines and planning window stickers and cup logos for identification. Finally, the group addressed lost cups, keeping the deposit at the one euro constraint, and reviewed action items before scheduling the next conceptual design meeting for next week.
predictions.SY0110c: The team reviewed dishwasher test results and agreed to use in-mould labelling and a moulded ribbed band on a single three-hundred-millilitre cup size in slate grey. They approved the counter return flow and reviewed a slate grey window sticker badge. Finally, they assigned action items for quotes, the badge design, and a staff guide, and agreed to wait for cost quotes before requesting more samples.
predictions.SY0110d: The team reviewed the moulding quote and agreed on an initial order of ten thousand units at one euro fifty-four per cup, sticking with slate grey for launch. They confirmed requirements like dishwasher safety and unit cost, and reviewed the final cup specifications and storefront badge. Marketing Expert agreed to contact cafe owners from the trade fair, Industrial Designer will confirm the order and request pre-production samples, Marta will laminate the staff guides, and Project Manager will write the final report and meeting minutes.
predictions.SY0202a: Marcus opened the kickoff meeting to design a library self-checkout kiosk under four thousand euros, leading the team to agree on core checkout and renewals using cards or app codes via a single reader. They discussed printed versus digital receipts and physical buttons versus touchscreens, before emphasizing accessibility. Priya agreed to gather accessibility requirements for Hannah, Tomas took on the component layout, Hannah will map out the checkout and renewal flow, and Marcus will circulate the project brief and meeting notes.
predictions.SY0202b: The team convened for their second meeting to discuss functional design, component layouts, and marketing findings favoring email defaults. They incorporated accessibility requirements, including a physical help button that activates audio mode, and decided to await RFID pricing before choosing a tracking method. Finally, Tomas agreed to sketch the casing appearance with new heights, and the project manager will share meeting notes and brief Hannah.
predictions.SY0202c: The project manager opened the third conceptual design meeting by recapping decisions on receipts, help buttons, and shelf heights, while Priya confirmed she had emailed accessibility notes. The team agreed to include both an RFID pad and barcode scanner on the kiosk. Tomas presented three casing sketches, and the team selected the desk-style unit with a tilted screen, opting for oak veneer with aluminium corners to reduce costs. Hannah presented updates to the user flow covering login, bulk book reading via RFID, renewals, and email receipts. The team discussed help button functions, deciding short press calls staff and long press starts audio mode, with Tomas taking on the text-to-speech engine and board selection, while keeping the fifteen-inch screen size. In closing, Priya agreed to base the evaluation criteria on the library services list, the project manager will circulate the updated cost breakdown, and the team plans to revisit screen size after reviewing the mock-up.
predictions.SY0202d: The project manager opened the final detailed design meeting, noting Hannah's absence and reviewing the agenda. Industrial Designer Tomas presented mock-ups, leading the team to compromise on a seventeen-inch screen and a licensed text-to-speech board. The project manager reviewed Hannah's screen designs, and Marketing Expert Priya presented evaluation scores across seven criteria, with cost scoring finalized at six after updating unit estimates. The team rejected adding an LED ring to the help button, reviewed action items, and scheduled the final report and tagging numbers before concluding the meeting.
predictions.SY0209a: The team held a kickoff meeting for designing a protective case for the Learnly seven-inch educational tablet, confirming the four-to-eight age range and deciding the case must be custom-fit for the Learnly device only. During brainstorming, they discussed drop protection, carry handles, bright colours, wipeable materials, and a potential name tag window. The project manager will write and circulate the minutes, and the next meeting is scheduled for half an hour later.
predictions.SY0209b: The project manager opened the second meeting, reviewing survey feedback on drop resistance and approving EVA foam for the body and corners. The team made decisions on child-friendly holding features, a fixed handle, and dropped ideas for a folding stand and swappable covers. Finally, they assigned tasks for sketches, cost estimates, and pricing checks, while deferring a discussion on colors to the next meeting.
predictions.SY0209c: The team reviewed survey results confirming drop protection and name tag windows as priorities, deciding on a shallow wedge, blue and lime green colours, and keeping two colours for launch while dropping a stylus slot. They noted the supplier's question regarding toy safety regulations and reviewed the total estimated cost, which remains comfortable under ten thirty even with a window insert. Finally, the meeting concluded after assigning tasks for the upcoming detailed design meeting.
predictions.SY0209d: The project manager opened the detailed design meeting by reviewing pricing and design features, and after initial safety checks were discussed, Tomasz led scoring evaluation criteria on a scale from one to seven. The team rejected a shoulder strap due to safety risks and added cost, and confirmed the foam pocket name tag design and a twenty-five euro price point. Finally, the project manager assigned action items for physical samples, drawings, and evaluation scores before concluding the meeting.
predictions.SY0304a: Hannah opened the kickoff meeting with Priya and Tom to design campus parking availability displays under a tight schedule. The team agreed displays should show space numbers and color codes for staff, students, and visitors, focusing on physical signs while deferring a mobile app. Hannah assigned Marcus to investigate sensing options and costs, Priya to survey campus users, and Tom to sketch layout sizes. Finally, Hannah agreed to circulate the minutes and project brief today.
predictions.SY0304b: The project manager reviewed survey results and sensor options before the user interface designer presented layout choices, leading the team to agree on a sixty-centimetre LED display with specific colour-coded thresholds. The group also agreed to use mains power from the barrier supply and selected barrier counters with a nightly reset, reducing the estimated cost to around four hundred per sign. Finally, the project manager agreed to check with the estates office about a central sign and assigned follow-up tasks before closing the meeting.
predictions.SY0304c: The project manager reviewed the central sign design with Tom, noting the layout features, solid red warnings, and a navy powder-coated aluminum casing. They discussed mains connections and a supply issue at the underground library car park, concluding that the budget remains tight with ten pounds to spare for the other four signs. Finally, the team assigned tasks for the next detailed design meeting, addressed barrier drift with a nightly reset, and decided to defer the QR code idea.
predictions.SY0304d: The team reviewed electrical quotes, mounting brackets, and sign layouts, assigning Tom to create five print-ready vector files for the name strips. They discussed counter drift, agreeing to maintain the nightly reset alongside spot checks by Priya in the first fortnight. Finally, the group evaluated the design against survey feedback and concluded the meeting by assigning final action items including booking the library electrician, drafting a campus newsletter entry, and submitting the report to estates.
